detail: 4 graph calls; 35 txns in episode window, 7 memory cases, 1 rare devices

rationale: The only anomalous element is the flagged transaction itself: $35.66 online, product C, from a Windows/chrome 66.0 browser marked New for the account, scored 0.76. Everything else in the 72-hour window is the cardholder's normal in-person 'W' activity in home regions 264/310/110 (34 in-person txns, 25 within 48h of the flag), so there is no paused-home-activity clone pattern, no burst of 2-4 online purchases, no tiny-authorization run and no just-under-threshold run. The amount is below the card's mean ($114.31, z = -0.37) and the card already has 21 online txns and 13 distinct devices in 180 days, so a previously unseen browser string is weak on its own. The card does carry three prior confirmed-fraud cases (CC-1475, CC-3216, CC-4294), which raises the prior and is why this is not dismissed outright, but all of those involved multi-transaction bursts or mixed-channel sprees rather than one small purchase. The rare device found by the shared-device query (SAMSUNG SM-G950U, 4 cards all-time) does not appear on this card's flagged transaction and produced no linked cards in the window. Under R1 this is a single signal below 0.70, so verification is required before any block; semantic memory (CC-3520, CC-4395, CC-5236) shows small new-device alerts of this shape closing as confirmed purchases.
